purpose: Finite generated-media checks for the initial compatibility and recoverable-damage scope. This pack does not certify every codec, browser, device, HDR profile, or corrupted file.

requires: Admission through the repository testing-memory workflow
An existing local FFmpeg runtime supporting lavfi, libx264, libopus, AAC, MPEG-TS, and fMP4 HLS
The registered guarded Docker helper or the existing admitted Linux local media helper
execution.asset_origin: Synthetic lavfi testsrc2 and sine signals; no network fixture downloads or user media
execution.asset_size: Eight seconds, 160 by 90 pixels, 24 frames per second, mono audio
execution.identity_evidence: DUSKCUE_COMPATIBILITY_RUNTIME logs the actual ffmpeg -version output, including build configuration and library versions
execution.result_evidence: DUSKCUE_COMPATIBILITY_CORPUS logs source BLAKE3 hashes, frame-hash count, exact damage byte/packet positions, surviving ranges, output progress, and expected unrecoverable failure
execution.cleanup: Only the UUID-owned compatibility subdirectory is removed on success or returned error; the shared fixture mount and other test assets remain intact

production_paths_exercised: build_ffmpeg_input_args using normal bounded probe defaults
build_stream_mapping_args_for_video with selected global video and audio indexes
StreamPlan.codec_args with independently copied or encoded video and audio
build_video_encode_args for the software recovery path
build_hls_output_args for finite EVENT fMP4 output
assertions: Clean copy routes retain all 192 decoded video frame hashes and publish H264 video plus AAC audio
Selected audio is audible and has the expected generated sine frequency
Recoverable damage permits useful video and audio after the known damaged GOP
Finite successful jobs publish media segments and ENDLIST
Missing essential MP4 metadata fails without publishing a playable media playlist
All generated source file hashes remain unchanged by packaging and decoding

fixtures.generation: Finite H264 yuv420p testsrc2, no B frames, fixed two-second GOPs, 440 Hz AAC mono audio, final MP4 moov
fixtures.expected: Completed decodable fMP4 HLS; original decoded video hashes and 440 Hz audio preserved
fixtures.limit: Exercises server packaging and decoding; it does not test HTTP direct-file serving or browser rendering

fixtures.generation: Copy the clean H264 elementary stream into Matroska and encode its 440 Hz audio as Opus
fixtures.expected: Completed H264/AAC fMP4 HLS with unchanged decoded video hashes and audible 440 Hz audio

fixtures.generation: Matroska global stream zero is 880 Hz Opus audio; stream one is copied H264 video; stream two is 440 Hz Opus audio
fixtures.expected: Copied video frame hashes match the clean reference; converted selected audio measures approximately 880 Hz rather than 440 Hz

fixtures.generation: Remux the clean H264/AAC source into constant-muxrate MPEG-TS; derive byte landmarks from ffprobe video packet timestamps normalized to the first video timestamp

mutation.damage: XOR the latter video PES payload bytes of one complete selected transport packet with 0xa5, preserving sync, transport/adaptation headers, and the PES prefix
mutation.truncation: Retain bytes preceding the first video PES transport packet at or after the landmark; keep transport-packet alignment
mutation.runtime_evidence: Exact byte ranges, video PID, normalized timestamps, and verified next clean keyframe are emitted for the actual FFmpeg build

fixtures.expected: Packaging completes the retained prefix; progress exceeds 5.5 seconds; a video frame decodes at 5.5 seconds and 440 Hz audio decodes at 5 seconds
fixtures.allowed_degradation: Visible artifacts or dropped frames around the damaged GOP and loss of the deliberately removed tail
fixtures.limit: One deterministic local corruption and tail truncation; not arbitrary missing headers, random corruption, growing downloads, or guaranteed reconstruction of missing frames

fixtures.generation: Parse the clean MP4 top-level atoms, require mdat before final moov, and retain only bytes preceding moov to model an unfinalized ordinary MP4
fixtures.expected: Command fails within the existing command deadline and produces no media-bearing HLS playlist
fixtures.limit: Missing essential metadata is an expected failure; this pack does not attempt forensic sample-table reconstruction or claim that fragmented MP4 behaves identically

deferred_matrix: HEVC Main10, AV1, VP9, and H264 Hi10P profile fixtures
HDR10, HLG, HDR10+, Dolby Vision profile handling, and color correctness
AC3, EAC3, DTS, TrueHD, multichannel downmix and object-audio passthrough
ASS/SSA styling, PGS/VobSub burn-in, forced subtitles and embedded fonts
MOV, WebM, AVI, MPEG-PS, M2TS, ASF/WMV, MPEG4 Part2, VC1 and interlaced MPEG2 variants
Bad timestamps, missing indexes, damaged Matroska cues and unsupported attached-picture layouts
Hardware decoder fallback, sustained bitrate limits, multiple simultaneous sessions and 4K performance
Actual browser/native client startup, seeking, track switching, playback recovery endpoint behavior and VLC/Kodi comparative qualification
Fuzzing, adversarial parser inputs, DRM, encrypted streams and disc menus
